content.title: What is a Fighting Illini? Explaining the origin of Illinois' nickname, mascot history | Sporting News
content.text: In an NCAA Tournament in which many familiar brands advanced to the Sweet 16, Illinois is as much of a newcomer as any team still standing.While the Illini have plenty of history as a men's basketball program, this is their first trip to the Sweet 16 since 2005. No. 3 seed Illinois' advancement through the bracket came fairly easily. Brad Underwood's team overcame an early challenge against No. 14 Morehead State in the first round, then made quick work of No. 11 Duquesne in the second round. That set up a daunting matchup with No. 2 seed Iowa State's tough defense.The Fighting Illini have hit their stride offensively in recent weeks, led by Terrence Shannon Jr.'s dominant scoring stretch. Could a Final Four berth really be on the table with reigning champion UConn in the same region?Here's what you need to know about Illinois' nickname, including where "Fighting Illini" first originated.TSN's MARCH MADNESS HQ:Live NCAA bracket news | TV schedule | Predictor toolWhat is a Fighting Illini?What is an Illini? The University of Illinois archives have the answers.Illini is believed to have originated as a reference to Native Americans, though the university says that is "open to interpretation." Whether or not the Illini nickname for athletic department originated as a reference to Native Americans, the term did also describe the Illinois Confederation, a group of 12 or 13 tribes that inhabited Illinois.For much of the university's history, however, Illini simply referred to the students and student-athletes at the school. An Illinois men's basketball player is a Fighting Illini because he plays for Illinois, and there isn't too much else to it beyond the word potentially originating as a reference to Native American tribes.Why is Illinois called the Fighting Illini?So, how did the term catch on? Per the university archives, "Illini" was first used in 1874 when the student newspaper renamed itself, adding that the first edition of the renamed newspaper implied that the name was new and "had not formally existed prior." "During the late 19th century and the first years of the 20th century, it was often used to refer to the students, faculty, staff and alumni as a whole," according to the university."Fighting Illini" wasn't used to describe Illinois' athletics teams until 1921. The term was evidently connected to military service, as it was used as a call for the construction of a new stadium "built to honor alumni, staff, and students who died during World War I." Illinois does not know the exact date that "Fighting Illini" was formally adopted as the school's athletics nickname, but it's believed to have happened between 1921 and 1930.DeCOURCY: Re-ranking the Sweet 16 teamsIllinois Fighting Illini mascotIllinois currently does not have a mascot. The school did have a de facto mascot from 1926 until 2007 in Chief Illiniwek, a Native American symbol representing the Illinois Confederation of tribes, also known as the Illini. Chief Illiniwek was played by a person in costume, though the person's face was visible.Chief Illiniwek was retired in 2007, two years after it was listed by the NCAA as one of 18 "hostile or abusive" mascots that could lead to punishment from the organization if continued. Illinois Sweet 16 historyThis year's Sweet 16 isn't exactly the most unique in NCAA Tournament history. Twelve of the 16 teams still standing reached the Sweet 16 in either 2022 or 2023, and all but four of the top 16 seeded teams advanced to the round.Illinois is an outlier. While the Fighting Illini had Sweet 16 expectations as a No. 3 seed, they haven't advanced this far since 2005. That's the longest drought of any of this year's Sweet 16 teams, easily longer than Marquette (11 years), NC State (9 years) and Clemson (6 years).There have been some close calls for Illinois, including a second round exit as a No. 1 seed in 2021. Brad Underwood's squad not only got over the hump this year but did it easily by coasting past Duquesne in a drama-free second round matchup.Here's a complete look at Illinois' past trips to the Sweet 16 and how each season turned out.YearResult1951Lost in Final Four1952Lost in Final Four1963Lost in Elite Eight1981Lost in Sweet 161984Lost in Elite Eight1985Lost in Sweet 161989Lost in Final Four2001Lost in Elite Eight2002Lost in Sweet 162004Lost in Sweet 162005Lost national championship2024TBD
